config.review.model: Id of the language model used by **Review with AI**. Run **Bitbucket: Select AI Review Model** to choose from the available models (e.g. GitHub Copilot).
config.review.instructionFiles: Glob patterns, relative to the repository root, of project rule files given to the AI review. Only read when the repository is open in VS Code.
config.review.language: Language of the comments written by **Review with AI**. **Auto** uses the VS Code display language.
config.review.excludeFiles: Glob patterns of changed files that the AI review skips, e.g. generated code.
config.commentFix.excludeAuthors: User names (or parts of display names) whose comments are left out by **Fix All Comments with AI**, e.g. review bots. Service accounts are always left out. **Fix with AI** on a single comment still works for them.
tool.getComments.userDescription: Reads the open review comments of your Bitbucket pull request.
tool.reply.userDescription: Posts a reply to a review comment after you confirm it.
welcome.jiraNotConfigured:
Sign in to Jira to see your tasks, check commit messages and create branches.
[Sign In to Jira](command:jiraBitbucketFlow.jira.configure)
welcome.notConfigured:
Get notified about new comments on your Bitbucket pull requests and reply to them from here.
[Set Up Bitbucket Connection](command:jiraBitbucketFlow.bitbucket.configure)
welcome.noPullRequests: You have no open pull requests and no pull requests to review.
config.jira.baseUrl: Jira base URL, e.g. `https://jira.example.com` or `https://your-team.atlassian.net`. Run **Jira: Set Up Connection** to set it together with your token.
config.jira.email: Atlassian account email. Only needed for Jira Cloud; leave empty for Jira Server/Data Center (personal access token).
config.allowedIssueTypes: Issue types that may be referenced in commit messages. Leave empty to allow any sub-task type.
config.onViolation: What to do when a commit message references an issue that is not assigned to you or has a disallowed type.
config.onViolation.warn: Show a warning and let you choose whether to commit anyway.
config.branchPrefixes: Branch name prefixes offered by **Jira: Create Branch from Task**.
config.bitbucket.baseUrl: Bitbucket URL, e.g. `https://bitbucket.example.com` for Server/Data Center or `https://bitbucket.org` for Cloud. Run **Bitbucket: Set Up Connection** to set it together with your token.
config.bitbucket.email: Atlassian account email. Only needed for Bitbucket Cloud.
config.bitbucket.pollInterval: How often (in seconds) to check your open pull requests for new comments and reviews. Only one VS Code window polls at a time.
config.readiness.rules: Rules that show whether your tasks are ready for development. Tasks in the **My Tasks** view turn green when all rules pass, red when a rule fails and yellow when only warnings fail. Expand a task to see the checklist. Instead of writing rules by hand, run **Create Readiness Rules with AI** and paste your checklist. Put the rules in the workspace settings (`.vscode/settings.json`) to share them with your team. See the README for examples.
config.readiness.rule.name: Text shown in the checklist.
config.readiness.rule.issue: Issue to check: `parent` (the story of your sub-task, default) or `task` (the task itself).
config.readiness.rule.field: Jira field name as shown in Jira (e.g. `Fix Version/s`, `Description`) or field id (e.g. `fixVersions`, `customfield_10100`). Without `matches` the field must not be empty.
config.readiness.rule.matches: Regular expression (case-insensitive). The rule passes when any value of the field matches, e.g. a version name, a component or a linked issue key.
config.readiness.rule.subtask: The issue must have a sub-task that meets all given conditions.
config.readiness.rule.subtask.type: Regular expression for the sub-task type name.
config.readiness.rule.subtask.done: The sub-task must be in a done status.
config.readiness.rule.subtask.assigned: The sub-task must be assigned to someone.
config.readiness.rule.when: Apply the rule only when this field is set (or matches `matches`), e.g. only for bugs.
config.readiness.rule.lowestUnreleased: Each version in `field` (e.g. `Fix Version/s`) must be the lowest version of the project that is not released or archived. Versions with a different format (e.g. `2.2.0` and `1.2.0-beta`) are compared separately.
config.readiness.rule.severity: `error` (default) turns the task red, `warning` turns it yellow.
command.hidePullRequestComments: Hide All Comments of This Pull Request
config.bitbucket.panelComments: Which pull request comments appear in the **Comments** panel. Hidden comments (**Hide This Comment**) come back when someone writes in the thread.
config.bitbucket.panelComments.involved: Only the ones that concern me
Comments on your own pull requests, and threads you took part in on the pull requests you review.
config.bitbucket.panelComments.all.detai: Every comment of every listed pull request.
